13.title: The Biglieri Group: 25 Years of Growth
13.content: Website and Invitations for The Biglieri Group
13.subtitle: The Biglieri Group
13.overview:
The 25 Years of Growth campaign celebrated The Biglieri Group’s legacy while introducing the foundation of its modernized brand. The visual system revived the company’s signature square motif, a form that reflects its roots in urban planning, attention to detail, and sharp professional services; a symbol of structure, balance, and the built environment they’ve helped shape. 

By blending design with smart automation, including a custom RSVP website, built using Squarespace and Python-based data processing, replacing manual guest tracking with an automated system that reconciled invite lists, categorized responses, and generated clear, real-time reports, achieving then both a memorable brand moment and an efficient operational rollout. The result was a launch that not only resonated with clients, stakeholders and staff but also demonstrated the creative potential of strategic design in driving process improvement.
13.context:
When The Biglieri Group prepared to celebrate its 25th anniversary, the leadership team saw an opportunity to align the milestone with the company’s evolving brand identity. The goal was to create a polished, engaging campaign that honoured the firm’s history while signalling its next phase of growth and modernization. 

As the in-house designer, I was tasked with leading the visual direction, design production, and technical systems for the anniversary launch, including invitations, event branding, a custom RSVP platform, as well as assisting on the creation of on-site visuals. The project became the catalyst for the full company rebrand that followed, laying the groundwork for the organization’s new design ecosystem.
13.problem:
As The Biglieri Group approached its 25th anniversary, the leadership team wanted to celebrate the milestone with a campaign that honoured the firm’s history while presenting a refreshed, forward-looking identity. 

The challenge was that there was no centralized system for visual production or event design, and the rebrand launch needed to happen on a short timeline, just months before the celebration. The company required a cohesive visual direction, an efficient way to handle invitations and RSVPs, and a professional, accessible presentation that reflected both its legacy and its evolution.
13.research:
I began by reviewing the company’s historical branding, past campaigns, and internal workflows. Conversations with leadership and marketing reinforced the importance of preserving “the square”, a long-standing symbol. This became a key constraint for the RSVP experience: any modernization needed to feel deliberate, composed, and aligned with the firm’s roots, rather than overtly promotional. 

In parallel, I analysed competitor and adjacent industry event websites to understand prevailing RSVP patterns and user expectations. By deconstructing high-performing examples, I synthesized best practices around clarity, trust signals, and form simplicity into a single, brand-appropriate solution. I also evaluated the RSVP flow itself to identify where users dropped off, what caused hesitation, and which signals increased commitment.
13.process:
The process was structured to balance speed, clarity, and brand integrity under a compressed timeline. Rather than treating the work as a series of isolated deliverables, I approached it as a unified system that could scale consistently across print, digital, and event touchpoints. 

I established a clear project framework with defined timelines and workflows, while developing a modernized visual system anchored in the square motif. Design, production, and technical execution progressed in parallel, including the launch of an automated RSVP website that replaced manual tracking with a reliable, real-time system. Ongoing collaboration with leadership, marketing, and production partners ensured alignment and enabled a confident, on-time rollout.
13.solution:
The 25 Years of Growth campaign delivered a complete, integrated brand experience that celebrated The Biglieri Group’s legacy while symbolizing its evolution into a modern, forward-thinking urban planning firm. The event’s visual identity revolved around the square and new logo, a timeless emblem of the firm’s approach to city building. 

Across digital and print platforms, the motif served as a flexible grid for imagery, text, and motion graphics, creating cohesion across every element of the campaign. Meanwhile, the custom-built RSVP automation tool streamlined logistics, giving the coordination team real-time data and freeing time for more meaningful engagement. The campaign united creativity, precision, and technology, establishing a model for how design can drive both brand experience and operational efficiency.
13.impact:
The 25th anniversary campaign successfully delivered both a high-quality event experience and a meaningful operational improvement. The automated RSVP system enabled strong attendance and simplified guest management, while the cohesive visual execution across print, digital, and on-site materials received positive feedback from clients, partners, and internal teams. 

Beyond the event itself, the campaign established a new standard for professionalism, organization, and design execution within the company. Leadership recognized the work as a clear signal of the firm’s evolving identity, and the systems, workflows, and visual foundations introduced during the project became the starting point for The Biglieri Group’s broader rebrand and design system transformation.
technologies: Design: Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign, Figma, After Effects
Development & Automation: Squarespace, Python, Microsoft Excel
Project Management: Kanban, Sprint Cycles
Accessibility & Standards: AODA and WCAG Compliance

13.codeSnippet:
"""
Compare a Squarespace RSVP CSV with an internal invited list and export a color-coded report.

OUTPUT:
- comparison_report.xlsx
  - Sheet: "Guest List" (all invited, color-coded)
  - Sheet: "Summary" (counts)

COLOR KEY:
- Green  : Coming
- Yellow : No response
- Red    : Not coming

REQUIREMENTS:
- pandas
- openpyxl

EXPECTED INPUT COLUMNS (configurable below):
- Internal list CSV: email
- Squarespace RSVP CSV: email, rsvp_status
  where rsvp_status values include (case-insensitive):
  - "yes", "coming", "attending"
  - "no", "not coming", "declined"
"""
import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.styles import PatternFill

# -------------------- CONFIG --------------------
INTERNAL_CSV = "internal_invited_list.csv"
RSVP_CSV = "squarespace_rsvp_list.csv"
INTERNAL_EMAIL_COL = "email"
RSVP_EMAIL_COL = "email"
RSVP_STATUS_COL = "rsvp_status"
OUTPUT_FILE = "comparison_report.xlsx"

COMING_VALUES = {"yes", "coming", "attending"}
NOT_COMING_VALUES = {"no", "not coming", "declined"}
# ------------------------------------------------

# Load CSVs with error handling
try:
    internal_df = pd.read_csv(INTERNAL_CSV)
    rsvp_df = pd.read_csv(RSVP_CSV)
except FileNotFoundError as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")
    exit(1)

# Validate required columns
if INTERNAL_EMAIL_COL not in internal_df.columns:
    print(f"Error: Column '{INTERNAL_EMAIL_COL}' not found in internal list")
    exit(1)
if RSVP_EMAIL_COL not in rsvp_df.columns or RSVP_STATUS_COL not in rsvp_df.columns:
    print(f"Error: Required columns not found in RSVP list")
    exit(1)

# Normalize emails
internal_df[INTERNAL_EMAIL_COL] = internal_df[INTERNAL_EMAIL_COL].str.strip().str.lower()
rsvp_df[RSVP_EMAIL_COL] = rsvp_df[RSVP_EMAIL_COL].str.strip().str.lower()

# Handle duplicates in RSVP data (keep most recent)
rsvp_df = rsvp_df.drop_duplicates(subset=[RSVP_EMAIL_COL], keep='last')

# Normalize RSVP status and handle NaN
rsvp_df[RSVP_STATUS_COL] = (
    rsvp_df[RSVP_STATUS_COL]
    .fillna("")
    .astype(str)
    .str.strip()
    .str.lower()
)

# Merge RSVP info onto internal list
merged = internal_df.merge(
    rsvp_df[[RSVP_EMAIL_COL, RSVP_STATUS_COL]],
    how="left",
    left_on=INTERNAL_EMAIL_COL,
    right_on=RSVP_EMAIL_COL,
)

# Determine final status
def resolve_status(status):
    if pd.isna(status) or status == "":
        return "No response"
    if status in COMING_VALUES:
        return "Coming"
    if status in NOT_COMING_VALUES:
        return "Not coming"
    return "No response"

merged["Final Status"] = merged[RSVP_STATUS_COL].apply(resolve_status)

# Summary counts
summary = merged["Final Status"].value_counts().reindex(
    ["Coming", "No response", "Not coming"], fill_value=0
).reset_index()
summary.columns = ["Status", "Count"]

# Write to Excel
with pd.ExcelWriter(OUTPUT_FILE, engine="openpyxl") as writer:
    merged.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="Guest List", index=False)
    summary.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="Summary", index=False)

# Apply colors
wb = load_workbook(OUTPUT_FILE)
ws = wb["Guest List"]

GREEN = PatternFill(start_color="C6EFCE", end_color="C6EFCE", fill_type="solid")
YELLOW = PatternFill(start_color="FFEB9C", end_color="FFEB9C", fill_type="solid")
RED = PatternFill(start_color="F4CCCC", end_color="F4CCCC", fill_type="solid")

status_col_idx = None
for i, cell in enumerate(ws[1], start=1):
    if cell.value == "Final Status":
        status_col_idx = i
        break

if status_col_idx:
    for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2):
        cell = row[status_col_idx - 1]
        if cell.value == "Coming":
            cell.fill = GREEN
        elif cell.value == "No response":
            cell.fill = YELLOW
        elif cell.value == "Not coming":
            cell.fill = RED

wb.save(OUTPUT_FILE)
print(f"Report generated: {OUTPUT_FILE}")

14.title: The Biglieri Group: Building a Smarter Design Ecosystem for Harmony and Efficiency
14.content: Design Systems and Environment for the Biglieri Group
14.subtitle: The Biglieri Group
14.overview:
When I joined The Biglieri Group, the firm was experiencing rapid growth but lacked visual and procedural cohesion across its branding and graphic materials. Hundreds of planning reports, figures, maps, and standalone graphics were being produced annually, each with inconsistencies in layout, typography, labeling, and accessibility. Reports were visually dense, graphics were often rebuilt from scratch, and planners relied on manual formatting that slowed delivery and increased the risk of errors. 

Rather than treating this as a surface-level visual refresh, I approached the work as a branding and systems problem. I led a comprehensive rebrand that unified visual identity, graphic standards, typography, and production workflows into a single, coherent framework. Working closely with leadership, planners, and office coordinators, a scalable design ecosystem was built, that strengthened brand clarity, improved the legibility of technical graphics, and dramatically reduced production friction across all deliverables.
14.context:
As The Biglieri Group entered a period of sustained growth, its leadership team recognized a growing disconnect between the quality of its planning work and the way that work was being presented. While the firm was delivering increasingly complex and high-impact urban-planning projects, its visual identity and production systems had evolved organically, resulting in  noticeable inconsistency across materials. 

The rebrand reframed the firm’s visual identity not as a surface layer applied at the end of production, but as an integrated system embedded directly into how planning work is visualized and delivered. Reports, figures, maps, and technical graphics were redesigned to speak a consistent visual language, one that reflects clarity, legibility, and confidence. Drawing on modernist and Swiss design principles, the new brand system introduced a refined typographic hierarchy, standardized grid systems, figure logic, and a restrained but purposeful colour palette. These elements were carried consistently across long-form reports, data-heavy diagrams, presentation decks, and standalone graphics, ensuring that every output reinforced the same brand signal, regardless of scale or author. 

Crucially, the rebrand was paired with deeply considered production systems. By embedding brand rules directly into templates, styles, and automation workflows, the new ecosystem enabled the company to produce brand-aligned, accessible documents without manual intervention or redesign. The result is a visual identity that not only elevated perception externally, but also improved efficiency, consistency, and confidence internally, setting a new standard for how the firm communicates its work.
14.problem:
At the document level, complexity had begun to work against clarity. Reports accumulated layers of manual fixes, figures followed different visual conventions, and uneven numbering and document readability. Small inconsistencies compounded across pages, turning otherwise rigorous planning work into visually dense and fragile deliverables. 

Without shared standards governing layout, typography, graphic structure, or accessibility, consistency depended heavily on individual effort. Planners spent valuable time adjusting spacing, labels, and formatting instead of focusing on analysis and narrative. Designers were often brought in late to correct presentation issues rather than shape clarity from the outset. As deadlines tightened, maintaining quality became increasingly difficult. 

The core issue was not a lack of expertise or care, but the absence of a system capable of supporting complexity at scale. The firm needed a way to embed brand clarity, accessibility, and production logic directly into everyday workflows, so that every report and graphic could meet the same standard without reinventing the process each time.
14.research:
To understand the root causes behind inconsistent outputs and production friction, I conducted interviews and workflow observations across planners, coordinators, and leadership. The goal was to examine not just what was being produced, but how documents, figures, and graphics moved from draft to delivery. 

The research revealed that inefficiency was rarely caused by the complexity of planning content itself. Instead, it emerged at the intersection of process and design, where manual formatting, version control issues, and disconnected tools created unnecessary back-and-forth between planners and designers and individuals tasked with formatting the final document. Hours were lost managing layout details, reformatting figures, and managing content within Microsoft Word, powerful yet limited tool for this specific task. 

These findings shaped a set of internal brand guidelines and working guides: tools designed to actively govern how work is produced and displayed across all mediums. The system unified custom document grids, a refined colour palette, a typeface family, shared iconography, and modular components. At its core was an automation workflow: planners write in Word using predefined styles, which map directly into Adobe InDesign templates where layout, hierarchy, numbering, tables of contents, and final visual polish are applied automatically.
14.process:
At the outset of the project, I established a structured delivery framework to support both design quality and speed. I brought in and directly managed a design consultant to support production across templates and system components, while maintaining clear creative direction and ownership of the overall system. 

Work was organized using a Kanban and sprint-based methodology, with Asana serving as the central project board. Tasks were broken into two-week sprints, with regular check-ins to review progress, validate outputs, and adjust scope as needed. This structure made it possible to track velocity, surface blockers early, and ensure that system decisions translated into tangible improvements across deliverables.
14.solution:
The Biglieri Group rebrand delivered a single, intelligent framework that unified brand expression, document structure, and production workflows across the organization. What was previously fragmented is now governed by a cohesive system that ensures every report, figure, and graphic aligns with the same visual and operational standards. 

Rather than treating design as a final layer, the solution embeds structure and logic directly into how work is created. Content, layout, and formatting are connected through standardized workflows that reduce manual intervention, improve accuracy, and maintain consistency by default. This shift transformed document production from a reactive process into a reliable, scalable system. 

By aligning branding with automation and workflow optimization, the solution elevated both the quality and efficiency of deliverables. The result is a design environment that supports clarity, credibility, and speed, allowing the firm to focus less on formatting and more on communicating complex planning work with confidence.
14.impact:
This project replaced fragmented design practices with a single, system-driven framework that now governs how The Biglieri Group produces its work. Design consistency is no longer dependent on manual effort, it is built directly into everyday workflows. 

Automated templates and style-mapped production reduced formatting time by approximately 71%, allowing teams to focus on content and analysis instead of layout and revisions. At the same time, reports, figures, and graphics now present a consistent, accessible, and professional brand across all deliverables. Beyond efficiency, the system improved reliability and scalability. Built-in standards reduced errors, ensured AODA and WCAG compliance, and created a repeatable production model capable of supporting growing project volume without added design overhead. 

This project was a great opportunity to lead a full-scale branding and systems initiative end to end. Beyond design execution, it required defining scope, managing a fixed budget, setting timelines, and communicating progress and outcomes across the company. I developed stronger skills in planning and leadership, creating clear scopes of work, running structured presentations and training sessions, and aligning stakeholders around long-term design decisions. Managing and directing additional designers taught me how to delegate effectively, assign work based on strengths, and ensure individual contributions supported a cohesive system rather than isolated outputs. 

Most importantly, the project reinforced the value of treating design as infrastructure. By focusing on systems, process, and clarity, I learned how to scale quality, empower teams, and deliver lasting impact beyond individual deliverables.
technologies: Design: Adobe Creative Suite (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop), Figma
Automation & Integration: WordsFlow, Python, Microsoft Office
Typography: FontForge (custom type family inspired by Swiss 721)
Accessibility & Standards: AODA, WCAG 2.1
